# Introduction {-}

<span style="font-size:xx-large;">DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS</span>

This free book will help you stop masturbating: right away, without misery, and without white-knuckling it. There are no cold showers, no rubber bands on your wrist, and no ninety-day streak counter to babysit.

You don't need to stop, or even cut down, while you read. In fact, please don't. Carry on exactly as you are until you reach the end of the book. Trying to quit halfway through only gets in the way.

That probably sounds backwards. Everything you've been told says the opposite: try harder, pray harder, hide the phone, reset the counter. Has any of it worked? If it had, you wouldn't be holding this book.

Ask yourself honestly:

- Have you quit porn but still masturbate to memories, fantasies or whatever crosses your feed?
- Do you do it more often than you meant to, or at times you swore you wouldn't?
- Have you made promises to yourself, or to God, that you broke within days?
- Do you reach for it automatically: in bed, in the shower, when you're bored, stressed, lonely or can't sleep?
- Do you feel flat, guilty or disgusted with yourself afterwards, and then do it again anyway?
- Do you keep it secret, and would you be ashamed if the people you respect knew how often?
- Do you find your thoughts drifting to it at work, in church, or while talking to a woman?
- Has it cost you energy, focus, sleep, motivation, or closeness with your wife or girlfriend?
- Have you ever counted days, reached a streak you were proud of, and lost it in five minutes?

If you answered yes to any of these, keep reading. That's all you need to do.

If you're reading this for a son, a husband, a brother or a friend, the best thing you can do is get him to read it. If he won't, read it yourself. Understanding how the trap works makes it far easier to help him out, and to keep the next generation from walking into it.

## About this book {-}

This book is a sequel.

If you've read *EasyPeasy* (the free hackbook *The Easy Peasy Way to Quit Porn*), you already know how this works. Maybe you've already used it to walk away from porn. Well done. That was the hard part, and you did it.

But many men find that once the porn is gone, something is still there underneath: the hand, the late-night itch, the shower routine, the reel of memories and fantasies that plays whenever you're bored or alone. You've escaped the harem. Now it's time for the next level: getting masturbation and lust out of your life for good.

Let's be honest about where this book comes from. We didn't invent anything. We took EasyPeasy's format, chapter by chapter, and applied it to masturbation. EasyPeasy was itself a rewrite of Allen Carr's *Easy Way to Stop Smoking*. The credit for the method belongs to them, and any mistakes in applying it here are ours. If you haven't read EasyPeasy and porn is still part of your habit, read it too ([easypeasymethod.org](https://easypeasymethod.org/)). This book works on its own, but the two belong together. Like EasyPeasy, this book is free and open, and anyone may copy and share it.

It works on one condition:

**DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS.**

Think of it as a staircase. Each chapter is a step, and each one only holds your weight because the one beneath it is there. Jump ahead to the "how to stop" chapter and you'll land on nothing.

Follow the steps in order and I can promise you this method is:

- **Immediate.** You don't taper off. You stop.
- **Just as effective** for the man who does it three times a day as for the man who does it twice a week.
- **Free of misery.** No weeks of climbing the walls.
- **Free of willpower.** You won't be gritting your teeth.
- **Free of gimmicks.** No apps, no supplements, no locked boxes.
- **Clean.** You won't swap this habit for overeating, scrolling, drinking or porn.
- **Permanent.**

You probably don't believe that. Neither did the men who've already walked out of this trap. Here are a few of them, in their own words:

> "I have been porn free for 10 years, and it has done wonders for my mental health… I am much more at peace mentally, and sexual sin like lust has become much less of a struggle."
>
> — a man on a Christian forum, ten years free

> "For eleven years, I would spend my days in a mental prison cell, one I didn't realize I was in."
>
> — a man who shared his story on a Christian recovery blog

> "I did notice a benefit of increased focus… I felt so much more like myself."
>
> — a YouTuber who went a year without it

## A word on faith {-}

This book is written from a Christian point of view. It says plainly what the Bible says: lust is sin. Jesus didn't set the bar at the act. He set it at the look: "everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart" (Matthew 5:28). Ask yourself honestly how often you've done this without picturing someone. For almost every man the answer is never. That is why this book calls it what it is.

But this book isn't a sermon, and you don't have to be a Christian to use it. If you're an atheist, play along. When the book mentions God or sin, read it as a man's conscience talking, or call it mindful self-talk if that helps. The method works the same either way. What you're about to learn about the trap is true whether or not you've ever set foot in a church.

## Warning {-}

If you're hoping this book will frighten you into quitting with talk of shrinking testosterone, hair loss, and how disgusting and weak you are, you'll be disappointed. Scare tactics have never freed anyone. If fear worked, you'd have quit years ago.

The usual methods ask you to use willpower: count the days, cut down to once a week, hide the phone, take a cold shower, and white-knuckle through the urges. Some sites will bury you in studies and claims. Some churches will bury you in guilt. None of it removes the reason you do it. Making something forbidden only makes it more precious, and the moment you weaken, you're back.

This method is different. Some of what you're about to read will be hard to believe. By the end of the book, you'll not only believe it. You'll wonder how you ever believed anything else.

Here's the first thing that will sound strange: **you never chose this habit.** Yes, you choose each time. You lock the door, you open the app, you start. But did you ever sit down as a boy and decide, "I'm going to do this every night for the next fifteen years, whether I want to or not"? Of course you didn't. Curiosity and puberty started it. A habit you never really chose took over from there, and for most of us, porn later poured fuel on it.

When did you decide that you couldn't sleep without it? That you couldn't handle a stressful day without it? That a night alone would be unbearable without it? You never decided any of that. It crept up on you.

You've fallen into a trap, and it is one of the most subtle traps there is, because the bait is your own body. No man who's caught in it wants his son caught in it too. That tells you everything. Every man in the trap wishes he'd never started, and yet every man in the trap carries on. Nobody forces him. So why does he do it?

## The only thing stopping you is fear {-}

What keeps you in the trap isn't desire. It's **fear**: the fear that stopping means an endless stretch of frustration, craving, restless nights and misery. It's built on beliefs you picked up along the way:

- "A man needs a release."
- "It's healthy. Doctors say so."
- "I'll go crazy if I don't."
- "It's the only thing that helps me sleep."
- "Everyone does it, and anyone who says they don't is lying."

Act on those beliefs for long enough and they produce exactly the life they predict. You feel you're owed it every night. You treat a day without it as a day of suffering. You wait for the next private moment. You look at women as material rather than as people.

So the fear grows. You fear the nights alone. You fear the hard days at work without your little reward. You fear that you'll never relax, focus or feel confident without it. Most of all, you fear that you'll never be completely free. You fear that this is just how men are, and that even if you stop, you'll spend the rest of your life fighting it. If you've already tried and failed several times, as most of us have, you won't just fear that. You'll be convinced of it.

If you feel nervous right now, as though the time isn't right, notice this: the habit doesn't relieve that nervousness. It causes it. The trap is built to keep you in, and when do you plan to get out? Tomorrow? Once you're married? After this stressful season? Stop kidding yourself. That day never comes by itself. This trap was built to keep you for good.

## The good news {-}

Here is the chicken-and-egg problem. Every man in this trap wants out, and every man can find it easy to get out. Only fear stops him. The greatest gain of all is losing that fear, but you won't lose it until you finish the book. It may even grow as you read, and some men put the book down halfway for exactly that reason. Don't be one of them.

You didn't choose to fall into the trap, but understand this: you won't climb out of it unless you decide to. You may be desperate to stop, or you may dread the very thought. Either way, remember: **YOU HAVE NOTHING TO LOSE.**

If you reach the end of this book and decide you'd rather carry on, nothing stops you. You don't have to cut down while you read. There's no shock treatment. There is only good news.

Remember the prodigal son? He was sitting in a pigsty, starving, when "he came to himself" (Luke 15:17). He got up and walked home, and he found a father running out to meet him. That's how it feels to walk out of this trap. By the end of this book, that's how you'll feel.

## Finally… {-}

Every man can find it easy to stop masturbating, and that includes you. Your only job is to keep reading, chapter by chapter, with your mind open. Every piece that clicks makes it easier. Even if you don't understand every word, follow the instructions and it will still work. You won't go through life feeling deprived or pining for it. By the end, you'll struggle to remember why you ever thought you needed it.

There are only two reasons this method fails:

1. **Not following the instructions.** Some men find this book annoyingly bossy about certain things, such as not cutting down and not using substitutes. Yes, some men have quit using those tricks, but they succeeded in spite of them, not because of them. And the instructions only work in order: one chapter after another, no skipping.
2. **Not understanding.** Don't take anything for granted. Question what you're told, including what this book tells you, and also what you've always assumed about sex, manhood and "needs". If you think it's just a habit, ask yourself why you can drop other habits easily but not this one. If you think you enjoy it, ask yourself why you can take or leave things you enjoy far more. Why do you *have* to have this? Why does panic set in at the thought of never doing it again?

You're about to do something every man in the trap secretly longs to do. You're going to be free, and you have every reason to look forward to it.

**DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS.**

### A few terms {-}

- **MO:** masturbation and orgasm, the habit this book is about.
- **The Little Monster:** the restless itch that says "go on, just do it". It's small, and it dies quickly once you stop feeding it.
- **The Big Monster:** the lies in your head that make the itch seem important. This book kills the Big Monster. The Little Monster then starves.

### How to read this book {-}

Don't read it like a novel. It's short, and you can finish it in a few hours. Many men find it helps to take notes or highlight as they go, and to read it a second time to make it stick.

Why a hackbook, and why a sequel? Because the method that freed so many men from porn deserves to reach the men who are still stuck with the habit underneath it. The author gains nothing from this, financially or otherwise.

There are communities for men walking this road, but check them out only after you've finished the book.

One last time: **DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS.**

I'd wish you luck, but you won't need it.

"If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed." (John 8:36)
